The density c/[y^2(log y)^2] normalizes with mean c; truncated second moments are O(b/log^2 b). With b_n=n/log^(3/2)n the exceptional maximum probability vanishes and Chebyshev gives S_n/(n/log n)->-c in probability, so null-test expectation vanishes. The centered integrable nonconstant walk hits every positive level; least deterministic quantiles N_j and Borel-Cantelli give T_j/N_j<=1 eventually. Supplied continuous densities leave positive mass at z, are jointly measurable, and yield KL(*)=2mu and KL(j)=2mu+1/N_j. Tilts have infinite mass but finite pointwise density and product exp(S_n-n/N_j); on nonrejection their integrals are uniformly <=exp(-a_n). Proper geometric prior and positive minimizer mass ensure finite positive evidence. At T_j, A_Tj>=exp(j-1)pi_j diverges, giving posterior limsup one. Type-I statistics do not vanish almost surely, so the stronger local theorem is unaffected. Repaired the parameter and alternative index sets to {1,2,...}: library N contains zero, while epsilon_j, density p_j and prior pi_j were defined only for j>=1.
